```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(infercalcR)
```

Two independent groups of fixed size, each with a binary outcome, give a
two-by-two table. Fisher's exact test conditions on both margins of that table.
Boschloo's unconditional test (Boschloo, 1970) uses Fisher's p-value only to
order the possible tables. Its p-value is the largest probability, over all
values of the common event probability under the null hypothesis, of a table at
least as extreme as the observed one. With the same sidedness convention,
Boschloo's p-value never exceeds Fisher's.

This tutorial computes Boschloo's test with infercalcR, compares it with
Fisher's test and looks at the rejection region of a design. The calculations
use only base R. One section uses the optional package digest and is evaluated
only when it is installed.

```{r optional-packages}
has_digest <- requireNamespace("digest", quietly = TRUE)
```

## The observed table

In this synthetic example, 2 of 12 patients respond in the control group and
8 of 12 in the treatment group. Rows are groups; the first column counts the
events.

```{r table}
responses <- rbind(control = c(response = 2, no_response = 10),
                   treatment = c(response = 8, no_response = 4))
responses
```

## Choose a variant before looking at the data

The two-sided alternative can be defined in two ways, and there are two
one-sided alternatives. `boschloo_variants()` lists the variants and how each
orders the tables.

```{r variants}
variants <- boschloo_variants()
variants[, c("variant", "alternative", "label")]
```

The `minlike` variant orders tables by the two-sided Fisher p-value. The
`central` variant doubles the smaller of the two one-sided p-values. Group 1 is
the first group passed to the function, so `less` means that the event
probability in group 1 is lower than in group 2.

## Compute the test

`boschloo_inference()` takes the event counts and group sizes and returns a
result in the common contract described in the
[getting-started tutorial](getting-started.html).

```{r boschloo}
boschloo <- boschloo_inference(x1 = 2, n1 = 12, x2 = 8, n2 = 12,
                               variant = "minlike", alpha = 0.05,
                               groups = c("control", "treatment"),
                               event = "response")
print(result_data(boschloo)[, c("estimand", "contrast", "estimate", "p.value",
                                "p.upper", "decision", "status")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```

The estimate is the observed difference in event proportions, control minus
treatment. The p-value is a supremum over the nuisance parameter and is found
numerically. `p.value` is the largest value attained by the search and
`p.upper` is a guaranteed upper bound for the supremum. The decision at the
stated `alpha` uses the upper bound. The bound describes numerical precision
only; it is not a confidence interval. The metadata state the assumptions.

```{r boschloo-metadata}
meta <- result_metadata(boschloo)
meta$assumptions
meta$numerical_bounds
boschloo$payload$native$fisher_p_value
```

The last value is Fisher's two-sided p-value for the same table, kept for
comparison. Boschloo's p-value is smaller here.

## The same test through a method specification

The Boschloo variants are also available through `method_spec()` and
`run_inference()`, which take the table directly.

```{r specification}
minlike_spec <- method_spec("boschloo_two_sided_minlike")
via_spec <- run_inference(minlike_spec, table = responses)
print(result_data(via_spec)[, c("estimand", "estimate", "p.value")],
      row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(result_data(via_spec)$p.value[1],
                           result_data(boschloo)$p.value)))
```

This result has one row for the test and one for the observed difference in
proportions. One-sided tests use `boschloo_one_sided` with the alternative
declared in the specification.

```{r one-sided}
less_spec <- method_spec("boschloo_one_sided", alternative = "less")
less <- run_inference(less_spec, table = responses)
result_data(less)[1, c("estimand", "p.value", "alternative")]
```

## Sidedness matters

The variants answer different questions. For this table the two two-sided
variants happen to agree, while the one-sided p-values depend strongly on the
direction. Choose the variant in the analysis plan.

```{r all-variants}
p_values <- vapply(c("minlike", "central", "less", "greater"), function(v) {
  result_data(boschloo_inference(2, 12, 8, 12, variant = v))$p.value
}, numeric(1))
round(p_values, 5)
```

## Compare with other exact tests

Fisher's exact test is available through the same interface and agrees with
`stats::fisher.test()`.

```{r fisher}
fisher <- run_inference(method_spec("fisher_exact_2x2"), table = responses)
print(result_data(fisher)[, c("estimand", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high",
                              "p.value")],
      row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(result_data(fisher)$p.value,
                           stats::fisher.test(responses)$p.value)))
```

Another unconditional exact test orders the tables by the pooled Z statistic
instead of Fisher's p-value. It requires an explicit statement that the two
groups are independent binomial samples.

```{r z-pooled}
z_pooled <- run_inference(method_spec("unconditional_exact_z_pooled"),
                          table = responses,
                          independent_binomial_groups = TRUE)
print(result_data(z_pooled)[, c("estimand", "estimate", "p.value")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```

## Operating characteristics of a design

For a planned design with 12 units per group, `boschloo_compare_fisher()`
compares the rejection regions of the two tests at the same nominal level. The
attained size is the largest probability of rejecting the null hypothesis over
all common event probabilities. Power is computed at event probabilities that
the analyst supplies.

```{r compare-fisher}
comparison <- boschloo_compare_fisher(n1 = 12, n2 = 12, alpha = 0.05,
                                      variant = "minlike", p1 = 0.2, p2 = 0.6)
comparison
```

For this design, every table rejected by Fisher's test is also rejected by
Boschloo's test. The additional tables bring the attained size closer to the
nominal 5 % and increase the power.

`boschloo_plotdata_lattice()` returns one row per possible table of the design,
with its Boschloo p-value and whether it is in the rejection region. The
observed table can be marked.

```{r lattice, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Grid of all 169 possible tables for 12 units per group. Filled squares mark tables in the Boschloo rejection region at the 5 % level; the observed table with 2 and 8 events is circled."}
lattice <- boschloo_plotdata_lattice(12, 12, alpha = 0.05, variant = "minlike",
                                     observed = c(x1 = 2, x2 = 8))
tables <- lattice$data
lattice$reference[c("attained_size", "n_rejected")]
plot(tables$x1, tables$x2, pch = ifelse(tables$in_region, 15, 0),
     xlab = "Events in group 1 (control)", ylab = "Events in group 2 (treatment)",
     main = "Rejection region, n = 12 per group", asp = 1)
points(tables$x1[tables$observed], tables$x2[tables$observed], cex = 2.5, lwd = 2)
```

## A complete test record

`boschloo_test()` returns the full record of the calculation, including the
numerical settings and a fingerprint of the specification. The fingerprint uses
digest.

```{r test-record, eval = has_digest}
record <- boschloo_test(2, 12, 8, 12, variant = "minlike", alpha = 0.05,
                        groups = c("control", "treatment"), event = "response")
record
```

The p-value is the maximum of the null probability of the tail set over the
common event probability. `boschloo_plotdata_nuisance()` evaluates that curve.

```{r nuisance, eval = has_digest, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Null probability of the tail set as a function of the common event probability. The curve peaks near 0.5 at the Boschloo p-value, shown as a dashed line."}
nuisance <- boschloo_plotdata_nuisance(record, grid_points = 201)
plot(nuisance$data$pi, nuisance$data$probability, type = "l",
     xlab = "Common event probability", ylab = "Null probability of tail set")
abline(h = record$p_value, lty = 2)
```

The record converts to the common contract with `as_inference()`.

```{r record-common, eval = has_digest}
common <- as_inference(record)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(result_data(common)$p.value,
                           result_data(boschloo)$p.value)))
```

The numerical tolerances of the search are set with `boschloo_control()` and
stored with every result.

```{r control}
boschloo_control()
```

## Reference

Boschloo, R. D. (1970). Raised conditional level of significance for the
2 x 2-table when testing the equality of two probabilities. *Statistica
Neerlandica*, 24(1), 1-9. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9574.1970.tb00104.x>
